chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If a piece is cut from a man, then it is carrion. So if a person touches it, then anything in which there is bone, ghusl becomes obligatory upon the one who touches it; but if there is no bone in it, then no ghusl is upon him.

key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: carrion; legally treated as dead flesh

ai.seo_question: Does touching a severed human body part require ghusl in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a severed part of the human body. It states that such a detached part takes the ruling of a dead body, and that touching it requires ghusl only when the severed piece contains bone.
